title: 第二十二章 春香楼第二十三章 码头的消息
content_zh:
：卯时三刻，天光微亮。
柳花巷的石板路上还残留着昨夜的湿气，几个宿醉的客人歪歪斜斜从春香楼侧门出来，被清晨的冷风一吹，扶着墙根吐了一地。
何成局从巷子东头走过来，穿一件洗得发白的青色短褐，袖口卷到手肘，露出两条被日头晒成麦色的手臂。他腰间系着一条黑色布带，脚上蹬着千层底布鞋，走得不快不慢。经过那几个醉汉时，他顺手把一个快要栽倒的胖子扶正了。
“王老爷，慢走啊，下次再来。”他笑着说，露出一口白牙。
胖子迷迷糊糊地摆摆手，被两个随从架着往巷口走了。
何成局推开春香楼的侧门。门内，几个杂役正在洒扫。一个瘸腿的老头拄着扫帚让开路，脸上堆着笑：“二当家，早啊。”
“老刘，昨儿腿疼没犯吧？”何成局停下脚步，从袖子里摸出个小纸包递过去，“茯苓堂买的狗皮膏药，我给你剪成了小块，贴的时候用火烤一下，粘得牢。”
瘸腿老刘双手接过，愣了一下。那膏药每帖都是铜板大的一片，边角修得圆圆的，怕毛边扎手。“二当家你这记性也太好了，我就随口提过一句……”
“废话少说，干活去。”何成局摆摆手，穿过大堂。
大堂里杯盘狼藉，空气中混杂着酒气、脂粉香和一股说不清道不明的暧昧味道。柜台后面，账房先生龚文已经坐在那里了。他今年六十整，瘦得跟竹竿似的，戴一副老花镜，算盘珠子拨得噼里啪啦响。
“二当家，早。”龚文头也不抬，全凭脚步声认人。
“早。”何成局在柜台边站定，自己动手从茶壶里倒了杯茶——照例是最便宜的粗茶，喝一口苦得舌根发麻。他皱眉，“老龚，你就不能换点能入口的茶叶？”
“能入口的茶叶要钱。”龚文推了推眼镜，把算盘一推，那张老脸从镜片后面抬起来，“昨晚上进账三两八钱。刨去柴米油盐和胭脂水粉，净亏六钱。幼楚姑娘喝醉了在二楼唱曲，多卖了三钱酒菜——算是唯一的意外之喜。”
“亏就亏吧。这阵子风声紧，能有进账就不错了。”何成局放下茶杯，“幼楚那丫头，让她少喝点——算了，说了也白说。”
楼梯上传来脚步声。
余三娘走下来。她今年四十七，穿一件暗红色的褙子，头发梳得一丝不苟，整个人干净利落得像一把刚擦过的刀。她在楼梯中间停了一下，看向何成局的目光跟看柜台上的茶壶没什么两样。
“二当家来了。”她说，语气里没有多余的温度。
“嗯。”何成局点点头，“昨晚上没什么事吧？”
“苏筱那个客人喝多了，吐在走廊里，刘二已经打扫干净。张颜差点跟客人吵起来，被林函拉开了。”余三娘走到柜台前，从袖子里抽出一张纸，“这是下半个月要采买的清单。”
何成局接过来扫了一眼。米面粮油、胭脂水粉、修缮屋顶的瓦片，每一项后面都标注了预算和几家对比的价钱。余三娘的字跟她的人一样，横平竖直，一笔不苟。

“就按这个来吧。对了，让厨房王婶多买些菜，晚上我请大家吃顿饭。”
“什么由头？”
“没由头。就是想吃了。”何成局笑着说，“让王婶多放辣椒。这几天嘴里淡出鸟来了。”
余三娘看了他一眼，接过清单转身就走。走出两步又回头，目光在他脸上停了一瞬。那目光很淡，却让何成局微微有些不自在——他知道她在看什么。三个月前那个深夜，他做了一件至今想起来都觉得心虚的事。那件事改变了一切。
事情要从六年前说起。
何成局十三岁那年被舅妈卖进了春香楼。
他记得那天舅妈拉着他的手走了很远的路，从城北的棚户区一直走到柳花巷。他以为舅妈是带他去走亲戚，路上还问他饿不饿，给他买了一个烧饼。到了春香楼门口，舅妈让他坐在大堂里等着，自己上楼去了。他坐在那张陌生的椅子上，脚够不到地面，晃着两条腿吃完了那个烧饼。
舅妈下楼的时候，身后跟着一个胖胖的中年女人——后来他才知道那是春香楼的老当家。舅妈从他身边走过，没有看他一眼，脚步很快，几乎是逃出去的。他叫了一声“舅妈”，舅妈没有回头。他想追出去，老当家一把按住了他的肩膀。那只手又肥又重，像一块五花肉压在他肩上。
“别追了。你舅妈把你卖给我了。三十两。”
他愣在那里，嘴里还含着最后一口烧饼。老当家上下打量了他几眼，捏了捏他的胳膊，又掰开他的嘴看了看牙口，像在牲口市场上挑骡子。“瘦是瘦了点，但骨架还行。打杂劈柴应该够用。会干活吗？”
他摇了摇头。他只会放牛，在舅舅家的牛棚里住了五年。舅妈嫌他能吃，早就想把他打发走。
“不会干就学。”老当家松开他的下巴，对旁边管账的一个年轻女子说，“三娘，带他去后院，让他先从倒夜香干起。”
那个叫三娘的年轻女子走过来。她那时三十出头，比现在瘦，也比现在爱说话。她蹲下来，平视着他的眼睛说：“我叫余三娘。你叫什么？”
“何成局。”
“何成局，从今天起你就在这儿干活。管吃管住，没有工钱。干得好，以后给你涨。”她站起来，领着往后院走。走了几步回头看了他一眼，那一眼里有同情，但更多的是审视——她在判断这个少年能不能撑过第一个月。
content_en:
: At three o'clock in the morning, the sky was slightly bright.
The moisture from last night still lingered on the stone pavement of Liuhua Lane. A few hungover guests staggered out of the side door of Chunxiang Building. They were blown by the cold morning wind and vomited all over the floor while holding on to the wall.
He Chengju walked over from the east end of the alley, wearing a blue and brown shorts that had been washed white. The cuffs were rolled up to his elbows, revealing two arms that were tanned by the sun. He wore a black cloth belt around his waist and wore thousand-layer cloth shoes on his feet. He walked neither fast nor slow. When passing the drunken men, he helped a fat man right upright who was about to fall over.
"Mr. Wang, walk slowly and come back next time." He said with a smile, showing his white teeth.
The fat man waved his hands in a daze, and was carried toward the alley by two followers.
He Chengju pushed open the side door of Chunxiang Building. Inside the door, several handymen were sweeping. A lame old man stepped out of the way with a broom and a smile on his face: "Good morning, Second Master."
"Old Liu, are you okay with your leg pain yesterday?" He Chengju stopped, took out a small paper bag from his sleeve and handed it over, "I cut the dog skin plaster I bought from Fulingtang into small pieces for you. When applying it, bake it over a fire to make it stick firmly."
The lame old Liu took it with both hands and was stunned for a moment. Each patch of plaster is a piece as big as a copper plate, and the corners are rounded to prevent rough edges from pricking your hands. "Second Master, you have a very good memory, so I just mentioned it casually..."
"Stop talking nonsense and get to work." He Chengju waved his hand and walked through the lobby.
Cups and plates were in a mess in the lobby, and the air was mixed with the smell of alcohol, powder, and an unexplainable ambiguous smell. Behind the counter, Mr. Gong Wen, the accountant, was already sitting there. He is sixty years old this year, as thin as a bamboo pole, wearing a pair of reading glasses, and the beads on his abacus are rattling.
"Good morning, Second Master." Gong Wen didn't even raise his head and recognized people solely by their footsteps.
"Morning." He Chengju stood at the counter and poured a cup of tea from the teapot - as usual, it was the cheapest coarse tea. One sip was so bitter that the root of the tongue was numb. He frowned, "Old Gong, can't you change to some tea that can be eaten?"
"Tea that can be imported costs money." Gong Wen pushed up his glasses, pushed the abacus, and the old face looked up from behind the lenses, "I made three or eight yuan last night. After excluding the firewood, rice, oil, salt, and rouge and gouache, I lost six yuan. Miss Youchu got drunk and sang on the second floor, and she sold three yuan more food and drinks - this is the only unexpected surprise."
"Let's take a loss. The wind is tight these days, so it would be nice to make some money." He Chengju put down the teacup, "That girl Youchu, let her drink less - forget it, it's all in vain."
There were footsteps on the stairs.
Yu Sanniang walked down. She is forty-seven years old, wearing a dark red gown, her hair is combed meticulously, and her whole body is as clean as a freshly polished knife. She paused in the middle of the stairs and looked at He Chengju as if she were looking at the teapot on the counter.
"The second boss is here," she said, without any extra warmth in her tone.
"Yeah." He Chengju nodded, "Did you have nothing to do last night?"
"The guest Su Xiao drank too much and vomited in the corridor. Liu Er has already cleaned up. Zhang Yan almost quarreled with the guest, but Lin Han pulled him away." Yu Sanniang walked to the counter and took out a piece of paper from her sleeve, "This is a list of purchases for the next half of the month."
He Chengju took it and glanced at it. Rice, flour, grain and oil, rouge, gouache, roof tiles for repair, each item is marked with a budget and comparative prices from several companies. Yu Sanniang's handwriting is the same as hers, horizontally and vertically, and meticulous.
"Let's do this. By the way, let Aunt Wang from the kitchen buy more vegetables, and I'll treat everyone to a meal tonight."
"What's the reason?"
"No reason. I just want to eat it." He Chengju said with a smile, "Tell Aunt Wang to add more chili peppers. I've been losing my temper these days."
Yu Sanniang glanced at him, took the list and turned around to leave. After taking two steps, he turned back and his eyes stopped on his face for a moment. That look was very light, butMaking He Chengju slightly uncomfortable - he knew what she was looking at. That night three months ago, he did something that still makes him feel guilty when he thinks about it. That event changed everything.
It started six years ago.
When He Chengju was thirteen years old, his aunt sold him into Chunxiang House.
He remembered that his aunt held his hand and walked a long way that day, from the shanty town in the north of the city to Liuhua Lane. He thought his aunt was taking him to visit relatives, and asked him if he was hungry on the way and bought him a sesame seed cake. When he arrived at the entrance of Chunxiang Building, his aunt asked him to sit in the lobby and wait while he went upstairs. He sat on the unfamiliar chair, his feet couldn't reach the ground, and swung his legs as he finished eating the sesame seed cake.
When his aunt came downstairs, there was a fat middle-aged woman following behind him—later he found out that she was the old head of Chunxiang House. Auntie walked past him without looking at him. She walked very quickly, almost running away. He called "Auntie", but Auntie didn't look back. He wanted to chase him out, but the old boss held his shoulders. The hand was fat and heavy, like a piece of pork belly pressing on his shoulder.
"Stop chasing you. Your aunt sold you to me. Thirty taels."
He stood there stunned, still holding the last bite of sesame seed cake in his mouth. The old boss looked him up and down, pinched his arm, then opened his mouth and looked at his teeth, like picking a mule at the livestock market. "I'm a little thinner, but my frame is still good. It should be enough for me to do odd jobs and chop firewood. Can you work?"
He shook his head. He only knew how to herd cattle and lived in his uncle's cowshed for five years. My aunt thought he was edible and wanted to send him away a long time ago.
"If you don't know how to do it, learn it." The old boss let go of his chin and said to a young woman who was in charge of accounting next to him, "Sanniang, take him to the backyard and let him start by pouring night fragrance."
The young woman named Sanniang came over. She was in her early thirties, thinner and talkative than now. She knelt down, looked into his eyes and said, "My name is Yu Sanniang. What's your name?"
"What a success."
"He Chengju, you will work here from today on. You will be responsible for food and housing, and there will be no wages. If you do a good job, you will get a raise in the future." She stood up and led him to the backyard. She took a few steps and looked back at him. There was sympathy in that look, but more of a scrutiny - she was judging whether the boy could survive the first month.
